What is an informal letter?

Great question! An informal letter is a friendly letter you write to someone you know well, like your friend, your brother or sister, your cousin, or your parents. Because you know the person, you can write in a warm, relaxed way, almost like talking. You can share news about school, ask about their health, or invite them to visit. It is different from a formal letter, which goes to someone like a headmaster and uses serious language. Think of someone you miss; an informal letter is a lovely way to reach them!

What are the parts of an informal letter?

Well done for asking! An informal letter has five main parts.

First, the writer's address at the top right corner, like 'No. 5 Adeola Street, Surulere, Lagos.'
Second, the date, written under the address.
Third, the greeting or salutation, such as 'Dear Ada,' or 'Dear Uncle Musa,'.
Fourth, the body, where you write your message in paragraphs.
Fifth, the closing, like 'Your loving friend,' followed by your name. Only one address appears in an informal letter, your own. Learn these five parts in order and letter writing becomes easy!

How do I start and end a letter to my friend?

Good question! Start with a friendly greeting like 'Dear Chioma,' with a comma after the name. Your first sentences can ask about their wellbeing: 'How are you? I hope your family is fine.' Then share your news. To end the letter, write a warm closing on its own line, such as 'Your loving friend,' 'Yours sincerely,' or 'Your cousin,' and then sign your first name under it. For example: 'Your loving friend, Kemi.' A friendly opening and a warm closing make your letter feel like a hug on paper. Try it today!

Where do I write my address and the date in an informal letter?

Nice question! Your address goes at the top right-hand corner of the page. Write it line by line, for example: 'No. 12 Ahmadu Bello Way,' then 'Kaduna,' then 'Kaduna State.' Directly under the address, write the date, like '9th July, 2026.' Remember, in an informal letter you write only your own address, not the address of the person you are writing to. The address and date tell your reader where the letter came from and when. After that, move to the left side and write your greeting. You are getting it!

What can I write about in a letter to my cousin?

Lovely question! You can write about anything friendly and interesting. Tell your cousin about your school: your new class, your best subject, or the inter-house sports competition. Share family news, like a new baby or a visit to grandma in the village. Describe something exciting, like the Sallah or Christmas celebration in your area. You can also ask questions: How is their school? Did they watch the last Super Eagles match? End by inviting them to visit during the holidays. Write as if you are chatting together under the mango tree. Enjoy your writing!

What is the difference between an informal letter and a formal letter?

Great question! An informal letter goes to someone you know well, like a friend or family member, and uses warm, friendly language. It carries only your own address. A formal letter goes to someone in an official position, like your headmaster, and uses serious, respectful language. A formal letter has two addresses, yours and the receiver's, plus a title or heading that states its purpose, and it closes with 'Yours faithfully'. An informal letter closes with things like 'Your loving friend'. Knowing which letter fits which occasion is a very useful life skill. Well done!

Can you show me a short example of an informal letter?

Of course! Here is a short one. Address and date at the top right: 'No. 7 Awolowo Road, Ibadan. 9th July, 2026.' Then the greeting: 'Dear Tobi,'. The body: 'How are you and your family? I am doing well. Our school held inter-house sports last week and my house, Blue House, came first! I ran in the relay race. I hope you can visit us during the long holiday so we can play together.' The closing: 'Your loving friend, Seun.' Short, warm and complete, with all five parts. Now write yours!

Why do we still write letters when we can just call or send a text message?

What a thoughtful question! Letters are still important for many reasons. A letter lets you organise your thoughts carefully and say everything you want without being interrupted. It can be kept for many years; some families still treasure letters written by grandparents long ago. Writing letters also trains you to write good compositions and prepares you for examinations, where letter writing is often tested. And when there is no network or the phone battery is flat, a letter still travels! Calls end in minutes, but a good letter can be read again and again. Keep writing!
